html:
The Kokomini, or Gugumini, are reported as an Aboriginal Australian people of inland Cape York Peninsula, on the upper Mitchell River. Some scholars think the name may cover a loose group of neighbouring clans rather than one people.

Their neighbours were the Kunjen downriver and the Kokowarra and Kuku Yalanji to the east. The Palmer River goldfield, opened in 1873, lay just to the northeast, and its miners and their supply routes brought violent clashes into this country.
